title: A `constructor` selection on an `any` receiver is dynamic code evaluation: `any` erases callability, so the rule fails closed
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx §Dynamic Features, the proposal recorded there under (IA-1): '`any` remains usable, but a receiver typed `any` in a position where the analysis must decide callability MUST be treated as callable — matching the fail-closed default already applied to a dynamically selected member.' THE HOLE WAS MEASURED, on both backends, and both implementations RECORDED it in their own comments before closing it — the fork's `dynamicCodeUse` said in as many words that a receiver typed `any` 'reaches neither arm ... That is the standing `any` hole ... The reference has the identical hole at the identical spelling.' `(JSON as any).constructor` compiled with zero diagnostics and an empty requirement row while the same selection on a resolved callable was SMITHERS1604. The cause is exact and is the reason this is a fail-closed fix rather than a widening: an `any` type has neither call nor construct signatures, so the callability test answered 'not callable' for the one receiver type about which NOTHING is known. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT USED TO: the migration plan lists it under R8 beside `WeakRef.deref()` and `Promise.race` as an UNMODELLED read. Once Flow bodies re-execute on replay, a nondeterministic read the compiler could not see produces two histories from one journal — and an `eval` reached through the `any` hole produces no journal entry, therefore no site-id mismatch, therefore no divergence to detect. That is why step 14 lands before the first production replay rather than after it. NO NEW DIAGNOSTIC CODE: this is the same operation SMITHERS1604 already names, reached through a receiver the rule previously declined to judge, so the code and its sentence are unchanged. BOTH SPELLINGS ARE HERE because they reach the `any` by different routes — an annotated binding and an assertion expression — and a fix keyed on the assertion alone would close one. `unknown` is deliberately NOT in this case and needs no case of its own: it must be narrowed before use, so the selection does not compile and stock TypeScript refuses the program before this rule is consulted. The positive control that keeps this narrow is the existing `the-function-constructor-is-dynamic-code-evaluation` pair and `host-global-allowlist.test.ts`'s 'an ordinary value's `constructor` is not the Function constructor', which pins that a RESOLVED non-callable receiver — an object literal, an array, a string, a `Map`, a class instance — is still free.
